reply.english: Yes, the building has a lift.
From the first of the month.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ. أهلين فيك
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaamu wa ra7matu Allaah. ahleen feek
dialogue.english: And peace and Allah's mercy be upon you. Welcome.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: عندي شقة حلوة كتير، قريبة من الجامع.
dialogue.english: I have a very nice flat, close to the mosque.

pair.english: How much is the monthly rent?
How many bedrooms does it have?

response.english: Yes, the building has a lift.

lessons.culture: In Damascus rent is quoted per month, and a deposit of about one month's rent is common. Ask whether the living room is counted among the rooms and whether water and electricity are included, and sign a written lease before paying anything.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فِي أَسَانْسِير؟" Say: yes, the building has a lift.

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says إي, أسانسير and العمارة.

exercises.tip: أسانسير is the everyday word for a lift, and عمارة for an apartment building.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "قدّيش الأجار بالشهر؟" Say: three hundred dollars a month.

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says تلاتميّة and بالشهر.

exercises.tip: ث often becomes ت in Damascene: تلاتة, تلاتميّة.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "قدّيش _____ بالشهر؟" (How much is the rent per month?)

too_formal.feedback: إيجار is the written word; people say أجار.

exercises.tip: أجار is rent; to ask the price, say قدّيش.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بدّي عقد أجار _____." (I want a one-year lease.)

too_formal.feedback: لمدة is written Arabic; speech says لسنة.

exercises.tip: لسنة means "for a year".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "How many bedrooms does it have?"
exercises.tip: فيها means "in it" and refers to the flat.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm looking for a flat to rent."

too_formal.feedback: أبحث عن is written Arabic; speech says عم دوّر على.

exercises.tip: عم + verb is "I am doing"; دوّر على means "look for".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can I view the flat?"

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says فيني شوف.

exercises.tip: فيني means "I can"; to a woman speaker nothing changes.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Is there a lift?"
exercises.tip: في here means "is there".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "How much is the monthly rent?"
exercises.tip: قدّيش asks "how much"; بالشهر means "per month".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Are water and electricity included in the rent?"

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says داخلين بالأجار.

exercises.tip: داخلين ("inside") is the everyday way to say included; شاملين is also understood.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Here are the keys of the flat."

too_formal.feedback: هذه is written Arabic; speech says هدول.

exercises.tip: هدول means "these" for several things, like keys.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Masha'Allah, very nice.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمّك. وفي كمان خزانة للتياب
dialogue.transliteration: walaa yhemmak. w fee kamaan khizaane lil-tyaab
dialogue.english: No problem. And there is also a wardrobe for clothes.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: I'll fix it, Allah willing.

pair.english: How many bathrooms are in the flat?
Where do I put the fridge?

lessons.culture: In Damascus the living room is usually called صالون and furniture عفش. A flat may be rented furnished or empty, so ask exactly what stays, such as the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioners, and check that the lights and appliances work before you sign.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "وين المطبخ؟" Say: next to the living room.

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says جنب الصالون.

exercises.tip: جنب means "beside"; صالون is the Damascene living room.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "كم حمّام بالشقة؟" Say: two bathrooms.

too_formal.feedback: حمّامان is the written dual; speech says حمّامين.

exercises.tip: The ending -ين makes the dual: حمّام becomes حمّامين.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "غرفة النوم _____." (The bedroom is spacious.)

too_formal.feedback: فسيحة is bookish; speech says واسعة or كبيرة.

exercises.tip: A feminine noun (غرفة) takes the feminine واسعة.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "وين خزانة _____؟" (Where is the wardrobe?)

too_formal.feedback: ملابس is written Arabic; Damascene says التياب.

exercises.tip: خزانة التياب is literally "the cupboard of clothes".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Is the flat furnished?"

too_formal.feedback: هل is written Arabic; speech just raises the voice.

exercises.tip: عفش is the everyday word for furniture.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I need a new bed."

too_formal.feedback: أحتاج إلى is written Arabic; بدّي covers "I want" and "I need".

exercises.tip: تخت is the everyday word for a bed.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The light doesn't work."

too_formal.feedback: لا يعمل is written Arabic; speech says ما عم يشتغل.

exercises.tip: ما عم + verb is "is not ... -ing".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "There is a sofa in the living room"?
exercises.tip: كنبة is a sofa; في means "there is".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Does the air conditioner work?"
exercises.tip: بيشتغل means "it works".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Put the table here."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says حطّ and هون.

exercises.tip: To a woman: حطّي الطاولة هون. هون is "here".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Where do I put the fridge?"

too_formal.feedback: ثلاجة is written; Damascene says براد.

exercises.tip: براد is the everyday Damascene word for a fridge.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, Yusuf.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: And peace and Allah's mercy be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Done, try the tap.

lessons.culture: A home repair is often a favour between relatives or neighbours before anyone is paid, and the helper is thanked with تسلم إيديك or الله يعطيك العافية. People say الحمد لله when a job ends well and إن شاء الله when they promise to try. A professional such as a plumber (سبّاك) or an electrician (كهربجي) is called when the problem is beyond a simple fix, and it is polite to ask the cost before the work starts.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فيك تصلّحو؟" Say: yes, I'll try.

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says إي and رح جرّب.

exercises.tip: جرّب means "try".

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تسلم إيديك، صار يشتغل هلّق." Reply.
exercises.tip: The fixed praise الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه is the same in every dialect.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الباب ما عم _____ منيح." (The door doesn't close well.)

too_formal.feedback: يُغلق is written Arabic; speech says يسكّر.

exercises.tip: سكّر is the everyday "to close / shut".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إذا لازم، اتّصل بال_____." (Call the plumber if needed.)
exercises.tip: A woman plumber is سبّاكة; an electrician is كهربجي.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The tap is leaking water."

too_formal.feedback: صنبور and يسرّب are written Arabic; speech says حنفية and عم تنزّ.

exercises.tip: نزّ means "to drip / leak"; مي is "water".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I need a hammer and nails."

too_formal.feedback: مطرقة is written; Damascene says شاكوش.

exercises.tip: شاكوش is the everyday word for a hammer.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "How much is the cost?"

too_formal.feedback: كم is written Arabic; Damascene says قدّيش.

exercises.tip: قدّيش is "how much".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "The power is out in the house"?
exercises.tip: راحت الكهربا means "the power went".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Pass me the screwdriver"?
exercises.tip: ناولني means "hand me"; to a woman: ناوليني.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "The lock is broken."
exercises.tip: Two words only: the noun, then مكسور.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "The light bulb doesn't work."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says اللمبة ما عم تشتغل.

exercises.tip: لمبة (a bulb) is feminine, so the verb is تشتغل.

reply.english: In the bin at the entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: And peace and Allah's mercy be upon you.

pair.english: Where do we put the rubbish?

response.english: In the bin at the entrance.

lessons.culture: In Islam a neighbour has a great right. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said that Jibril kept advising him about the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would be made an heir. In Damascus neighbours share food, visit one another when ill, keep an eye on each other's homes and try not to disturb each other with noise. Sending a dish to the new family next door is a common way to start a friendship.

exercises.prompt: A neighbour says: "جبتلكن شوي أكل." Thank him with the usual blessing.

too_formal.feedback: A correct fixed formula; this exercise practises the Damascene blessing الله يجزيك الخير.

exercises.tip: To a woman: الله يجزيكي الخير.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تعا اشرب شاي عنّا." Say: if Allah wills, another time.

too_formal.item: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، فِي وَقْتٍ آخَر
too_formal.feedback: Correct, but speech says مرّة تانية.

exercises.tip: مرّة تانية means "another time".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "فيني استلف _____؟" (May I borrow a ladder?)

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic with an ending; speech just says سلّم.

exercises.tip: سلّم is a ladder (also stairs).

exercises.prompt: Complete: "جبتلكن شوي _____." (I brought you some food.)

too_formal.feedback: طعام is written Arabic; speech says أكل.

exercises.tip: أكل means food or eating.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "We are your new neighbours."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says نحنا and جيرانكن.

exercises.tip: الجداد is the Damascene plural of جديد.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where do we put the rubbish?"

too_formal.feedback: نفايات is written Arabic; speech says الزبالة.

exercises.tip: منحطّ is the Damascene "we put".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Our neighbour is ill, we will visit him."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says تعبان and رح نزورو.

exercises.tip: تعبان means both tired and ill.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "I apologise for the disturbance"?
exercises.tip: A woman says آسفة.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "A neighbour has a right over us"?
exercises.tip: إلو حقّ means "has a right".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Which flat do you live in?" (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; speech says إنت ساكن.

exercises.tip: To a woman: إنتِ ساكنة.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Could you move your car, please?"

too_formal.feedback: هل and من فضلك are written Arabic.

exercises.tip: لو سمحت is the everyday "please / excuse me".

challenge.title: Viewing a flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a short conversation of at least 10 lines in Damascene. Ask about a flat for rent, its bedrooms, floor and monthly rent, ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, and say what you will take.
required_elements: a question about the rent or the number of bedrooms using قدّيش or كم
a question about the floor, the lift or whether water and electricity are included
a request to see the flat using فيني
a question about the kitchen or the furniture using وين or مفروشة
a closing decision with رح آخدها or بدّي عقد أجار

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. عم دوّر على شقة للأجار. قدّيش الأجار بالشهر؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. 3am dawwer 3ala sha22a lil-ajaar. addeesh il-ajaar bish-shahr?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I'm looking for a flat to rent. How much is the rent per month?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. تلاتميّة دولار بالشهر، وفيها تلات غرف نوم.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. tlaatmiyye dolaar bish-shahr, w fiiha tlaat ghuraf noom.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Three hundred dollars a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Which floor? And is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.transliteration: biT-Taabe2 it-taani, w fee asanseer bil-3imaare.
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and the building has a lift.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.transliteration: feeni shoof ish-sha22a? w hiyye mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Can I view the flat? And is it furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تفضّل. فيها عفش كامل، والمطبخ جنب الصالون.
dialogue.transliteration: tfaDDal. fiiha 3afsh kaamel, w il-maTbakh janb iS-Saaloon.
dialogue.english: Come in. It has full furniture, and the kitchen is next to the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Where do I put the fridge? And does the air conditioner work?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: البراد عند باب المطبخ، والمكيّف بيشتغل منيح.
dialogue.transliteration: il-braad 3ind baab il-maTbakh, w il-mukayyef byishtaghel mnee7.
dialogue.english: The fridge goes at the kitchen door, and the air conditioner works well.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: كتير حلوة، رح آخدها. بدّي عقد أجار لسنة.
dialogue.transliteration: ktiir 7ilwe, ra7 aakhedha. baddi 3a2d ajaar la-sane.
dialogue.english: It's very nice, I'll take it. I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تمام. بتدفع تأمين أجار شهر، وبتنتقل من أول الشهر.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. btidfa3 ta2meen ajaar shahr, w btinti2el min awwal ish-shahr.
dialogue.english: Fine. You pay a deposit of one month's rent, and you move in from the first of the month.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And you too.
